section_header: EMISSION CONTROL SYSTEMS — Exhaust Gas Recirculation (EGR) System
title: CHECK EGR VALVE / INSPECTION OF EGR VACUUM MODULATOR / INSPECTION OF VSV

content.description: Illustration showing EGR valve assembly with vacuum hoses connected

items: (a) Apply vacuum directly to the EGR valve with the engine idling.
(b) Check that the engine runs rough or dies.
(c) Reconnect the vacuum hoses to the proper location.

content.text: IF NO PROBLEM IS FOUND WITH THIS INSPECTION, THE SYSTEM IS OKAY. OTHERWISE INSPECT EACH PART

content.description: Illustration showing EGR vacuum modulator with engine stopped, port Q indicated

items: (a) Disconnect the vacuum hoses from ports P, Q and R of the EGR vacuum modulator.
(b) Block ports P and R with your finger.
(c) Blow air into port Q. Check that the air passes through to the air filter side freely.

content.description: Illustration showing EGR vacuum modulator with engine at 2,500 rpm, port Q indicated

items: (d) Start the engine and maintain engine speed at 2,500 rpm.
(e) Repeat the above test. Check that there is a strong resistance to air flow.
(f) Disconnect the vacuum hoses to the proper locations.

content.text: If a problem is found, replace the EGR vacuum modulator.
1. CHECK VACUUM CIRCUIT CONTINUITY IN THE VSV BY BLOWING AIR INTO PIPE

content.description: Illustration showing VSV connected to battery with terminals connected

items: (a) Connect the VSV terminals to the battery terminals as illustrated.
(b) Blow air into a pipe and check that the VSV is open.

content.description: Illustration showing VSV with battery disconnected

items: (d) Blow air into a pipe and check that the VSV is closed.

content.text: If a problem is found, replace the VSV.
